study type: Retrospective cohort study (secondary analysis of a national questionnaire study)
exposure: Grade of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASIS) in the first delivery (fourth-degree vs. third-degree tear)
Mode of second delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean)
cohort: The study included all Danish women who had an obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASIS) in their first delivery and one subsequent delivery, both occurring between 1997 and 2005.
finding: Women with a fourth-degree OASIS in their first delivery had a significantly higher risk of long-term anal and fecal incontinence after a second delivery compared to those with a third-degree sphincter injury.
mod_finding: The mode of second delivery was not significantly associated with the risk of long-term anal or fecal incontinence in women with a fourth-degree OASIS, nor did its effect differ between women with fourth-degree and third-degree injuries.
followup_time: Median 8.5 years since the second delivery (minimum 5 years)
